title: Budget Focus: Pay Equity, Dental, Early Retirement
summary:
*   City officials held a comprehensive worksession to discuss the upcoming operating and capital budgets, reviewing financial documents and departmental spending.
*   Mayor Cooksey requested more information on several key budget priorities, including a dental health program, a computer mapping initiative, staff development, and the crucial issue of pay equity.
*   Discussions also explored the potential costs and options for early retirement plans, while the City Manager challenged the accuracy of a proposed AFSCME plan due to insufficient data.

OPERATING AND CAPITAL BUDGET
City Manager Carrasco discussed outplacement activities and said he would give
Councilmembers a weekly report.
Virginia Rutledge, Director of Finance, went through the make-up of the budget documents.
Mayor Cooksey discussed the budget options and asked for more information concerning
dental health program, computer mapping program, :

Human Resource staff development program, participation figures for Pioneer Farm, transfer
liability reserve fund, and pay equity. Mayor Cooksey also wanted to know if there has
been a study of the AFSCME plan. Mr. Carrasco said the plan submitted by AFSCME had

Mayor Cooksey asked about early retirement plans. Ms. Rutledge discussed such plans and
said they can be extremely costly, but they are studying options and will report back to
Council.
Council then asked City Clerk Aldridge about the budget for the Clerk's office. Jorge
Carrasco discussed the City Manager's office budget; and various members of the
Communications Department answered questions about their budget for the coming fiscal
year. ADJOURNMENT Council adjourned its meeting at 5:35 p.m. )
